items.title: Buddy Collette interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: Nicolo from Verona, a guy that does jazz there, he said, “Who can you bring here that would get a big crowd?”

ctx.x: He didn’t want to go back to re-visit something.

Yeah. He liked Chico and they liked each other but he didn’t want to go with any of that anymore. Well I understand in a way, it was a big switch. I went back only because I set this up when I was in Europe. Nicolo from Verona, a guy that does jazz there, he said, “Who can you bring here that would get a big crowd?” And I was just being as truthful as I could by saying, “Well I could bring my group but in order to get a big crowd you’d do better with the Chico Hamilton quintet because the band never got to Europe…

were playing before. So he got excited right then. He said, “You think you can get him?” I said if I can talk to Chico to do it, because Chico’s not playing that way now. He only plays that way if we meet up. But he likes doing that. In fact he wanted just to do that, he and I would go to Europe, and play like that every night. I said no because I’d lose too much, meaning that after a while you want some other horns to come in. But we can do that in between.
